title: Return from the scheduler guessing phase
statement: Let $S$ and $V$ be finite deterministic Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x$ and $u$ be Boolean words. If $c$ is a configuration of $S$ on input $x$ whose state is absent, then for every bit $b$, one step of the reverse-host machine from the guessing-phase configuration determined by $c$ and $u$ produces the configuration in which the host is in its assembly phase, the assembly buffer contains the concatenation $xu$, and its head is at position $|xu|-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ and $V$ are finite deterministic Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet
replaced: Let $S, V$ be deterministic machines, $d$ a halted scheduler configuration on an input $x$, and $u$ a guessed word. For any choice bit, one host step from the guessing-phase configuration for $(d,u)$ yields the assembly-rewind configuration holding the assembled word $x\,u$ with assembly head at its last cell.
